[_Nym and Pistol draw._] Oh, alas, Our Lady, if he isn't drawing his sword now! We'll see deliberate adultery and murder committed.

BOY. Yes, he did. He said they were devils incarnate.

KING HENRY. So, by your rule, if a son is sent by his father on a trading voyage and dies sinfully at sea, the blame for his wickedness should fall on the father who sent him. Or if a servant, carrying a sum of money on his master's orders, is attacked by robbers and dies with many sins unforgiven, you could call the master's business the author of the servant's damnation. But this is not so. The King is not bound to answer for the particular endings of his soldiers, any more than the father for his son or the master for his servant. They do not intend their death when they intend their service. Besides, no king, however spotless his cause, can settle it by the judgment of swords with soldiers who are all spotless. Perhaps some carry the guilt of planned and plotted murder. Some have seduced virgins with the broken seals of perjury. Some are making the wars their shelter after they have wounded the gentle breast of Peace with pillage and robbery. Now if these men have cheated the law and outrun the punishment at home, though they can outstrip men, they have no wings to fly from God. War is his officer, war is his vengeance. So these men are punished, in the King's quarrel now, for breaking the King's laws before. Where they feared death, they escaped with their lives, and where they thought themselves safe, they perish. Then if they die unprepared, the King is no more guilty of their damnation than he was guilty before of the wickedness for which they are now visited. Every subject's duty belongs to the King, but every subject's soul is his own. So every soldier in the wars should do as every sick man in his bed: wash every speck out of his conscience. If he dies that way, death is a gain for him. If he does not die, the time was blessedly lost that bought such preparation. And in the man who escapes, it would be no sin to think that, because he made God so free an offer, God let him outlive that day to see His greatness and to teach others how to prepare.
KATHARINE. Is it possible that I should love the enemy of France?
KATHARINE. I cannot tell what that is.
KATHARINE. I do not know that.
KATHARINE. Your Majesty has _fausse_ — false — French enough to deceive the most _sage demoiselle_ — wise young lady — that is _en France_ — in France.
KATHARINE. That is as it shall please _le roi mon père_ — the king my father.
KATHARINE. Then it shall also content me.
